node_definition.done_when: Read section 12 of the-obligations-hook-reads-a-snapshot first. One correction to its mechanism: each sweep runs on its own thread, and _run_obligation_sweep in reckon/crew/runs.py already releases the sweep lock in its finally clause. What actually failed was every sweep, for as long as the record stayed unreadable, because stored_record in reckon/crew/review.py raised json.decoder.JSONDecodeError out of read_review into obligations._sub_floor_items_by_session and obligation_snapshot.fleet_state. Review workers write their record files themselves, so a reader can always meet a partial one. Make stored_record skip a record that does not parse and return what it can read, never raising. The snapshot built by reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py carries the skipped path as a finding, with the path and the parse error, so the reader sees it. A failure for one session inside obligation_snapshot.sweep is caught there, logged with its traceback, and does not stop the other sessions' snapshots; do not change reckon/crew/runs.py, which another run holds. In the same files, fold in the three follow-ons from section 11's review, recorded in followup f-tohras-008. Remove resolve() from reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py if nothing imports it. Gate the new-session worker-slots fallback on the admission block being present, not on sessions_present. Correct plan-verifies and evidence-commit in docs/evidence/fragments/the-obligations-hook-reads-a-snapshot/stop-hook-reads-the-snapshot.html to name sections 3 and 11 and the landed commit 87759a6e6. tests/test_unreadable_review_record_is_reported.py, in a temporary configuration home, plants a truncated review record beside a valid one. It asserts that a sweep publishes a snapshot carrying the valid record's duty and a finding naming the truncated path. It also asserts that a sweep raising for another reason leaves the next sweep free to publish. tests/test_obligations_hook_reads_the_snapshot.py, tests/test_stop_hook_reads_the_snapshot.py and tests/test_coordinator_obligations_hook.py keep passing; grep tests/ for stored_record and read_review to build the rest of the gate. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/the-obligations-hook-reads-a-snapshot/unreadable-review-record-is-reported.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line as revision= followed by the full sha, and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
